idiom_name: Slick Query.forUpdate inside .transactionally (or Doobie raw FOR UPDATE)
implementation_notes: Slick exposes forUpdate on Query - documented as 'specify part of a select statement for update and marked for row level locking' - and it takes effect when the action runs inside a transaction (DBIO.seq(...).transactionally); raw-SQL layers such as Doobie send SELECT ... FOR UPDATE directly. The row lock still ends at commit, so the offline lease is a lock record claimed and released by a small lock manager; the classic structure is what lets the lock survive between the HTTP requests that make up one business transaction.
pitfalls: forUpdate is only meaningful inside .transactionally; executed standalone (autocommit) the lock is released before the next action.
Locking the business row instead of the lock record serialises normal reads and writes of that row and still disappears at commit - the offline lease needs the record.
Slick runs DBIO on a bounded execution context; blocking Await.result(db.run(...)) while a connection waits on a row lock can starve the pool.
